article.headline: Numeric Style Codes Carry a Blueprint Aesthetic into AI Video
article.lede: Midjourney, the AI image-generation service, lets users steer visual style through numeric codes appended to any prompt — a single number that reproduces a coherent aesthetic across entirely different subjects. The post demonstrates code 3743853584, which yields a meticulous technical-drawing style, applied here to *Midjourney Video V1*, the service's first video generation model. A Coca-Cola can rendered as an engineering schematic is the test subject; the style, not the brand, is the point.
article.body:
The **--sref** parameter (short for *style reference*) was introduced to solve a persistent frustration: users would see a compelling image but lack the vocabulary to describe its visual qualities to an AI. Instead of requiring that description, Midjourney lets you attach a reference — either an uploaded image or, in shorthand, a numeric seed. That seed encodes a position in Midjourney's style-vector space; with over 4.2 billion possible values, the codes function less like options in a menu and more like coordinates on a vast aesthetic map.

The code 3743853584 corresponds to what the poster calls a 'meticulous schematic aesthetic' — something between an engineering blueprint and a product cross-section diagram. Rendering a Coca-Cola can in this style produces precise line work and annotated geometry, the vocabulary of industrial illustration rather than photographic realism. The style travels intact to any subject; whether you prompt 'a cat' or 'a city skyline,' the underlying visual grammar stays constant.

What distinguishes this post is the pairing with *Midjourney Video V1*. Applying a style reference code to video extends the consistency promise from a still frame to a sequence — the aesthetic persists across motion. Most discussion of sref codes has focused on still images; the transferability of a numeric style code into temporal media is an early proof-of-concept that the system's design is format-agnostic.

Communities have formed around cataloguing and trading these codes. At least one library claims over 4,800 v7 codes with new entries added weekly. The act of sharing a code rather than a prompt or a technique represents a compressed form of artistic knowledge transfer: unlike a verbal style description, which degrades in translation, a numeric code is exact. The limitation is opacity — you cannot inspect what a code encodes the way you might read a recipe.

concepts.definition: A numeric parameter added to a Midjourney prompt (e.g. --sref 3743853584) that applies a consistent artistic style to any generated image or video. The number acts as a coordinate in Midjourney's style-vector space, allowing artists to share and reproduce a specific aesthetic without describing it in words. Over 4.2 billion possible codes exist.

The first publicly available video generation model from Midjourney, allowing the platform's prompt-based tools — including style reference parameters — to be applied to animated sequences rather than single still frames.

A visual style drawn from engineering and technical illustration: precise line work, annotated geometry, cross-section diagrams, and blueprint-like composition. In AI-generated imagery, it refers to outputs resembling technical drawings or industrial schematics rather than photographs or painted art.
